_comment: Tier-2 for skfem wave#3, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / numpy 1.26.4. Claim: mass.assemble returns a csr_matrix and .sum(axis=1) gives a numpy.matrix on numpy<2, so use np.asarray(...).ravel(); signalled by TypeError 'unsupported operand type(s) for /' on the M_lumped division line, or a matrix-subclass DeprecationWarning. Ran: a 4x4 MeshQuad.init_tensor with ElementQuad1 (25 DOFs), M.sum(axis=1) under catch_warnings, ndarray / matrix, and a wave acceleration computed both ways. Printed: the TYPE half is right -- a numpy.matrix of shape (25, 1) -- but BOTH QUOTED SIGNALS ARE ABSENT: no TypeError and an empty warning list. Instead the (25,) ndarray broadcasts against the (25,1) matrix and silently returns a (25, 25) matrix. Worse, using that object as the inverse lumped mass STILL returns a length-25 vector, so a shape check passes, while the values are 1.97e+01 away from the correct elementwise division, with no warning. np.asarray(...).ravel() gives the (25,) array whose entries sum to the domain area 1.000000. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 takes the row sum as s = np.asarray(M.sum(axis=1)).ravel(), the documented fix, instead of the raw M.sum(axis=1). Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 14 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'rowsum_is_np_matrix=True', 'rowsum_shape=(25, 1)', 'division_result_is_N_by_N=True', 'division_silently_broadcasts_to_a_matrix=True' and 'wrong_acceleration_still_length_N=True' (and emits 'FAIL:'), so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
